page: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is a high-density compute-optimized server instance belonging to the Dldsv7 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Hardware-level acceleration is supported via Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which optimize vector and matrix operations.

The instance is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This allocation represents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing raw compute density over memory capacity. However, it includes a substantial local storage allocation of 11,339 GB and supports Premium Storage. The system lacks dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on the CPU for parallel processing tasks.

Benchmark results place the D192lds_v7 in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 202,853.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 152,145.2. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching top-tier speeds of 688.55 GB/sec for large-block read operations. Database and caching performance are also exceptional, with Redis SET operations achieving 268.62 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 157.94 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core performance is moderate, and text generation for small LLM models falls into the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D192lds_v7 offers high compute and local storage density, making it a viable alternative to memory-heavy instances for workloads that do not require large RAM footprints. It is highly suited for multi-threaded compute workloads, high-throughput web serving, large-scale database operations, and CPU-bound batch processing. The inclusion of AMX instructions also makes it capable of handling specific CPU-based machine learning inference tasks, such as prompt processing for large language models.
